chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'People say that the inner part of the two ears is from the face, and their backs are from the head.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is neither washing nor wiping upon them.'

key_terms.بَطْنُ الْأُذُنَيْنِ: The inner part of the two ears

ai.seo_question: Do the ears need to be washed or wiped during wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) resolves a juristic dispute regarding whether the inner and outer parts of the ears belong to the face or head by ruling that neither washing nor wiping is required, thereby exempting them from the specific ritual actions applied to those areas. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise anatomical boundaries in fiqh, distinguishing between the obligatory washing of the face and the wiping of the head. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the limits of wudu in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
